trapFamily.trap: vendor shape in the port, both ways: the e-signature vendor's envelope draft, envelope, recipient statuses and error codes leak into the outbound port and the sending and reminder logic, and its webhook event types and callback-handler signature (InkwellWebhookHandlers) become the shape the core receives callbacks in

subGoals.rule: Outbound: what the application asks of the signature service is written in the application's own language; the vendor's envelope draft, envelope, recipient fields, statuses and error codes stay in the adapter (Cockburn P1: each adapter talks to the application through a port).

Inbound: a vendor callback reaches the application as the application's own outcome; the vendor's webhook event types, event codes and callback-handler signature stay in the driving adapter, which checks the signature and translates (Cockburn P1, the driving side).
The core has no runtime dependency on the vendor SDK: a refused email, a busy service and a bad callback signature reach it, if at all, as its own errors or answers (Cockburn P1).

precedent: clean-shaped: the existing signing-allowance port (application/ports/out/AllowanceSource.ts) is written in the application's own type (SigningAllowance: remaining, renewsOn: Date), and InkwellAllowanceAdapter translates from the SDK's account() answer (planCode, envelopesRemaining, billingCycleEndsAt with an offset) into it. There is no inbound precedent: no callback is handled yet.

gaming.what: rename: the port declares its own copies of the vendor's envelope draft and envelope (emailSubject, documentBase64, routingOrder, sentDateTime, recipientStatus) under domain-sounding names, the service declares its own copy of the vendor's handler interface (SigningCallbacks with onRecipientDeclined / onEnvelopeExpired / onEnvelopeCompleted) and is handed to the SDK's dispatch, and vendor errors are recognised by e.name === 'InkwellError' and their errorCode strings
